audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Warwick, and the content prose supports the packet at every disputed stage.
audit.why: whys[0] says Warwick is a dashless melee who gives nothing back at level 1 — a Gnar stage, not Skill. whys[5] literally calls the first-item stage 'a coin-flip' (Skill, not Gnar). whys[6] and late both say he out-scales the duel — that is a Warwick stage, and the page currently marks it Gnar.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Warwick, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spikes said 'Stridebreaker'; Warwick's real spikes were never dated.
audit.why: Infinite Duress at 6 is 110s at rank 1 — long enough to plan whole windows around. Blood Hunt starts at 80s and only reaches 40s at rank 5, so his chase threat is far weaker early than the page implies. Your own first-item spike here is anti-heal, not Stridebreaker.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now names Bramble/Executioner's as the actual first-item swing, matching the content spikes[3] entry that already says so.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Infinite Duress as unavoidable ('Mega-peel it', 'Get R-suppressed', 'never commit Rage while his R is up') and never states that it is a CHANNEL. It also never mentions Primal Howl at all, and never states that Jaws of the Beast is percent-MAX-health.
audit.why: Both flagged missing interactions land here and they invert the advice. Infinite Duress is channelled, so Gnar's own hard CC — Mega Wallop or GNAR! — cancels it outright rather than merely surviving it; that turns his ultimate from a death sentence into a free kill window if Mega is banked. Jaws of the Beast scaling on max health means armour stacking reads the trade wrong, which matters because the itemization block currently points at Plated Steelcaps. Primal Howl is a 15s damage reduction plus a 1s fear and is entirely absent — it is the reason a committed brawl fizzles.
audit.corrected: Stated the channel cancel, the percent-max-health Q, Primal Howl's 2.5s damage reduction into a 1s fear, and Eternal Hunger's below-50%/below-25% healing tiers.

audit.whatIsWrong: content early, mid and late slip into first person ('are mine', "I'm", 'my', 'me').
audit.why: Breaks the second-person voice used everywhere else on the site.
audit.corrected: Converted to second person, same length band.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Land Infinite Duress' and 'Blood Hunts' as probable wrong names. Both are false positives: Infinite Duress is the correct R name and 'Blood Hunts' is the correct W name used as a verb. No name change proposed — but the verbed form is being removed anyway as part of the mid voice rewrite.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are mine: Warwick is a dashless melee, so my ranged Mini autos plus one Boomerang slow win the first trade for free, and at 2 a Hyper third-hit proc on top of a Boomerang is a chunky shove he can't answer before his Q heal and Blood Hunt come online. Don't over-extend chasing the chip, though: once Blood Hunt triggers on a low target he gets a burst of move speed, and his Eternal Hunger passive heals him harder the more HP you've taken. Poke, slow with Q, kite with Hyper's speed, and watch your Rage bar so you're never caught flat in Mini.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours: Warwick is a dashless melee, so your ranged Mini autos plus one Boomerang slow win the first trade for free, and at 2 a Hyper third-hit proc on top of a Boomerang is a chunky shove he can't answer before his Q heal and Blood Hunt come online. Don't over-extend chasing the chip, though: Blood Hunt triggers once you drop below 50% and gives him move speed toward you, and Eternal Hunger heals him below 50% HP and triples that below 25%. Poke, slow with Q, kite with Hyper's speed, and never sit flat in Mini.

edits.before: This is the even stretch and it's all about form timing versus his R. With Mega up, a Wallop stun or a GNAR! wall-combo flips any fight he tries to start, but if I'm stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he Blood Hunts in, I'm a fragile ranged target with no escape and his drain eats my poke. At 6 his Infinite Duress is the swing: it dashes in and suppresses me clean through the Mini-to-Mega transition, so never commit Rage while his R is up. Trade on his R cooldown, bank small leads, and rush anti-heal to keep his Q and passive from erasing my chip.
edits.after: This is the even stretch and it's all about form timing versus his R. With Mega up, a Wallop stun or a GNAR! wall-combo flips any fight he tries to start, but stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when Blood Hunt brings him in, you are a fragile ranged target with no escape. At 6 Infinite Duress is the swing: it suppresses you for 1.5 seconds clean through the Mini-to-Mega transition — but it is a channel, so a banked Wallop or GNAR! cancels it mid-leap. Hold Rage for exactly that, and rush anti-heal so his Q cannot erase your chip.

edits.before: Late, Warwick edges me: he's a drain bruiser who only gets scarier with healing and bruiser items, while my form-dependent burst plateaus and my solo dueling falls off. His missing-HP Eternal Hunger passive and Q mean a long fight always favors him, and Infinite Duress is a guaranteed lockdown that ignores my kiting entirely. My value shifts to the teamfight: GNAR! into a wall is one of the best engage-and-peel tools in the game, so stop trying to 1v1 his drain and instead flip his dive onto my team. Keep anti-heal up all game.
edits.after: Late, Warwick edges you: he's a drain bruiser who only gets scarier with healing and bruiser items, while your form-dependent burst plateaus and the solo duel falls off. Eternal Hunger and a percent-max-health Q mean a long fight always favors him, and stacking armour does nothing about either. Your value shifts to the teamfight: GNAR! into a wall is one of the best engage-and-peel tools in the game, and it also cancels his R channel, so peel his dive onto your team. Keep anti-heal up all game.

notes: The biggest correction here is that the page told the reader to fear Infinite Duress and 'never commit Rage while his R is up' — the opposite of the truth. It is a channel: Mega Wallop or GNAR! cancels it outright, so banking Rage FOR his ultimate is the win condition, not avoiding it. That reversal is now in tldr, winCon, phases[4].why, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, mid and late. Also added Primal Howl, which the page never mentioned once despite being a 15s damage-reduction-into-fear that decides committed brawls, and corrected the itemization implication that armour answers a percent-max-health Q. Packet suspectNames were both false positives. Not verified: whether cancelling Infinite Duress mid-channel refunds any of its cooldown, and whether Gnar's Hop can carry him out of the suppress radius before the leap connects.
